skills.trigger: When evaluating interval changes in a mediastinal mass and associated airway deviation between pre-operative and post-operative chest radiographs.
steps: Identify the location and extent of the mediastinal opacity on the baseline image, noting specifically if it causes displacement of the tracheal air column away from the midline.
Examine the follow-up image to assess the change in the width or density of the mediastinal opacity compared to the baseline.
Trace the tracheal air column on the follow-up image to determine if it has returned to a central midline position or remains deviated.

Correlate the reduction in mass size with the resolution of tracheal deviation to confirm successful intervention, distinguishing this from scenarios where mass size decreases but deviation persists (suggesting fibrosis or incomplete relief) or where deviation resolves without mass reduction (suggesting technical artifact or positioning change).
